evidence: Tardigrade CAHS/TDP genes raise desiccation tolerance in yeast, bacteria and cultured cells and a patent claims transgenic drought-tolerant plants, but the only plant work found is a 2025 Arabidopsis/agroinfiltration manuscript with inconsistent expression and no field or whole-crop pause-and-resume demonstration.

Tardigrade CAHS D plus trehalose has been shown (DARPA-funded, Sci Rep 2023) to stabilise dried human Factor VIII, and freeze-dried/trehalose-loaded platelets exist separately, but no work was found applying tardigrade glass-forming proteins to platelets for transfusion.

CAHS proteins protect HeLa and insect cells against osmotic/desiccation stress and gel reversibly on drying, but the EU DRYLIFE project concluded dry-state mammalian cells need many further changes, and no dried-and-revived mammalian cell bank was found.

Dsup reduces radiation-induced DNA damage in human cells and has been expressed in tobacco pollen (UV-B) and reportedly rice, but no Dsup transgenic seed, dried glassy state or sealed-capsule space-storage demonstration was found.

ETH Zurich demonstrated DNA encapsulated in dry silica glass with Reed-Solomon coding and accelerated-aging readback (millennia-scale projections), and Imagene's commercial process dries DNA and laser-welds it into inert-atmosphere metal capsules; only the tardigrade-protein matrix is new.

DNA-origami-placed plasmonic nanoparticle assemblies have been demonstrated as unclonable optical authentication labels (Dass/Liedl), and non-DNA optical PUF tamper-indicating seals exist, but no seal whose optical signature changes on opening via unfolding origami was found.

Gene-edited skin grafts that report a blood analyte by fluorescence have been demonstrated in mice: CRISPR-edited glucose-sensing skin as accurate as a blood test, and NF-kB-driven EGFP 'living skin' reporting internal inflammation; human versions are the stated next step.

Portable bedside EEG BCIs using motor imagery for covert awareness exist (mindBEAGLE) and have been tested in ICU disorders-of-consciousness patients and in EEG-fNIRS case reports, though accuracy and protocol length are still limiting.

Closed-loop optogenetic seizure control has been demonstrated in rodents with implanted optrodes and wireless seizure-detection-triggered light delivery that shortens seizures; no human implant exists, and human-usable opsins remain a translation barrier.

In situ partial reprogramming of mouse cutaneous wounds (OSKM induction) reduced myofibroblasts, contraction and scar, and a topical four-factor reprogramming solution healed ulcers in mice; only the timed peel-away mesh and human use are untested.

iPSC-derived skin with hair follicles, sebaceous and sweat glands has been demonstrated: RIKEN's 3D iPSC skin grafted into mice with follicles and glands, and UQ's 2024 human iPSC skin organoids with follicles, neurons and sweat glands; not yet in burn patients.

Universal platelets have been made at scale from beta-2-microglobulin-knockout iPSCs, and Kyoto's turbulence-driven VerMES bioreactor produced ~100 billion platelets per run with donor-comparable function in animal models; the open part is siting a cartridge in a hospital.

Partially decellularized rat kidneys reseeded with human endothelium perfused and made urine for ~90 min, and human discarded-kidney scaffolds have been seeded with hPSC endothelium, but no pig organ re-endothelialized with recipient cells and transplanted was found.

RNA-free mitochondrial editors work in vivo: AAV-delivered DdCBEs install mtDNA edits in adult mouse heart, AAV mitoZFNs shifted heteroplasmy with molecular and biochemical rescue in the m.5024C>T mouse, and a 2025 paper reports base-editing correction of a pathogenic mtDNA mutation in mice.

Topical dsRNA (UQ BioClay) sprays have protected plants against several viruses including aphid-transmitted ones, with dose-dependent ~60% resistance in tomato and reported glasshouse and field trials against zucchini yellow mosaic and tomato spotted wilt virus.

Peanuts with major storage-protein allergens removed exist: RNAi lines with significantly reduced IgE binding to Ara h 2/6, Clemson CRISPR lines edited at Ara h1/2/3/6 confirmed by IgE blots and basophil activation, and an AgriNetica CRISPR line in a first US field trial.

RNAi works in the salmon louse by immersion and injection (up to ~97% knockdown) and a patent describes salmon feed coated with dsRNA-expressing algae against louse COPB2, but no demonstrated louse-count reduction from oral dsRNA feed was found.

An ONR-funded Essex project is developing self-repairing engineered-biofilm hull coatings, UNSW encapsulated the antifouling bacterium Pseudoalteromonas tunicata in a 'living paint' lab prototype, and a 2025 paper assembles non-GM biofilm coatings, but field durability is unsolved and no working self-renewing coat exists.

Coral's own GFP fluorescence drops days before visible bleaching and is used as a non-invasive field indicator, but transgenic Symbiodinium reporters remain irreproducible and transient (1998 GUS work largely unrepeated), so no engineered sentinel colony exists.

Bacterial self-healing concrete that seals cracks by microbial calcite precipitation is real and commercially demonstrated, but no fluorescent or GFP-tagged reporting of repair sites was found; healing is still assessed visually, microscopically or ultrasonically.

An EBRC roadmap case study proposes releasing engineered algae with increased carbon capture and sinking biomass, and ballasted-particle export (Gigablue, mineral ballast studies) is being measured, but no organism engineered to make heavy indigestible shells for carbon export was found.

A 2025 proteomics study showed pore-size-based therapeutic apheresis lowers several age-associated plasma proteins, and a patent proposes columns for 'pro-aging' factors beyond the existing Kaneka Lixelle beta-2-microglobulin column, but no designed-binder affinity column targeting specific ageing factors has been demonstrated.

Reprogramming cochlear supporting cells into hair cells has been demonstrated in adult mice with a small-molecule/siRNA cocktail, and intratympanic drugs for the same job have reached humans (UCL's gamma-secretase inhibitor LY3056480, ISRCTN59733689; FX-322); only the weeks-long sequenced pump is new.

Designed amelogenin-derived peptides (LRAP with pyrophosphate; P26/P32 in chitosan hydrogel; QP5) have regrown organized enamel-like aprismatic layers on human enamel in vitro/ex vivo, and peptide remineralization products are already sold; no human trial of full enamel regeneration exists.

Gut-bacterial enzyme pairs convert the A antigen to H/O on intact red cells at low enzyme doses (Flavonifractor plautii, Nat Microbiol 2019; newer Akkermansia muciniphila enzymes stripping A and B extensions), though conversion of group A is still incomplete and no inline transfusion cartridge was found.
